checkpoints: When start is invoked, loading becomes true, checkCount increments, and checkPreparation is called for the captured token.
A PENDING result must not append the token to completed or otherwise signal delivery.
A PENDING result must arrange another check through the public retry scheduler.
A READY result must stop the pending cycle, set loading false, append the corresponding token to completed, and publish the resulting state.
DownloadDialog must continue exposing visible and loading through its existing data attributes and imperative preparation handle.
Public syntax/build checks are required after any implementation, but they do not establish the polling behavior.
forbidden_effects: Do not treat PREPARATION_STATUS.PENDING (false) as completion or delivery.
Do not append a token to completed before PREPARATION_STATUS.READY is received for that preparation cycle.
Do not change BackgroundExportPanel or useBackgroundPreparation as part of the file download dialog repair.
Do not replace scheduled retry behavior with a synchronous tight loop.
Do not modify tests, configuration, or the preparation service status contract.
Do not infer cancellation, coalescing, timeout, or latest-request-wins rules that are not established by TASK or public source.
lifecycle_identity: Each preparation check captures state.current.token as requestToken before calling checkPreparation; its result and any retry continuation must remain associated with that captured token.
The public dialog lifecycle includes start, close, and reopen(nextToken); reopen changes the current token, makes the dialog visible, and begins a check.
The sources do not establish whether an older pending cycle must be cancelled, retained, or superseded when reopen starts another token, so that policy must not be invented in this Contract.
Existing close only changes visibility and does not explicitly cancel an already-started request; whether retries must continue while closed is not expressly resolved by TASK.

obligations.text: Update the DownloadDialog preparation path so a PENDING status continues checking instead of ending the preparation attempt.
Use the public schedulePreparationRetry boundary to defer each follow-up check after PENDING, avoiding synchronous recursive polling.
Signal completion/delivery only after checkPreparation returns PREPARATION_STATUS.READY for the request token; in the supplied public model, that signal is the token being added to completed.
Keep loading true while preparation remains pending and clear it when the corresponding preparation becomes ready.

Preserve the existing initial start and reopen entry points, their token selection, visibility behavior, checkCount accounting, snapshot copying, and state publication except where pending retry requires additional checks.

Confine the business change to the file download dialog implementation path represented by DownloadDialog and usePreparation; the already-polling background export path is outside the requested change.

ordering_barriers: Capture requestToken before initiating checkPreparation so the returned status is attributed to the request that produced it.
After PENDING, schedule a later retry; do not perform completion bookkeeping before that retry chain reaches READY.
After READY, clear loading and record completion before publishing the completed snapshot.
A retry callback must begin the next check only when the scheduler invokes it.
preservation: Preserve DownloadDialog's use of usePreparation(token), its forwarded imperative handle, and its data-visible and data-loading surface attributes.
Preserve usePreparation's start, close, reopen, and snapshot interface.
Preserve close setting visible to false and reopen assigning nextToken, restoring visibility, publishing, and initiating a check, absent explicit evidence authorizing other lifecycle changes.
Preserve snapshot's defensive copy of completed.
Preserve PREPARATION_STATUS values and checkPreparation transport behavior.
scope: Business code for the file download dialog: src/DownloadDialog.jsx and its preparation hook src/usePreparation.js.
The public retry/status service in src/preparation-api.js may be consumed through its existing exports; its contract is not to be redesigned.
src/BackgroundExportPanel.jsx and src/useBackgroundPreparation.js are comparison evidence and outside the requested migration scope.

Public evidence does not define cancellation, overlap ownership, unmount behavior, retry limits, error handling, deduplication, or a delivery side effect beyond completed-token bookkeeping.

diagnoses.explanation: The behavioral Contract does not need revision. TASK expressly requires repeated checking while pending and delivery only after READY, and the public API already supplies distinct PENDING/READY values plus a retry scheduler. The original usePreparation implementation ends every resolved check by clearing loading and publishing; on PENDING it neither records completion nor schedules another check. That is a direct implementation gap against O1, O2, and O4. The previous candidate adds scheduler-based continuation and keeps the captured request token across retries, so the supplied failed acceptance verdict alone does not establish a further defect or justify changing the Contract. Syntax observations establish parsing only, not business correctness.
remaining_unknowns: The failed acceptance verdict supplies no public failure cause, so no additional candidate defect can be inferred from it.
No public source specifies close/unmount cancellation behavior, overlap policy, retry limits, rejection handling, or completion deduplication.
No concrete delivery side effect is publicly defined beyond adding the ready token to completed.

routing_analysis.contract: For the file download dialog, start or reopen begins an asynchronous preparation attempt for a captured token. Each check publishes loading and increments checkCount. PENDING must retain the attempt without completion and arrange the next check through schedulePreparationRetry. Only READY may clear loading and add that token to completed, with state published afterward. Existing dialog surfaces and lifecycle entry points remain intact. Background export behavior is outside scope. Close, overlap, cancellation, timeout, rejection, deduplication, and latest-request-wins policies remain unspecified.
